clue.text: Rubbish ballad finally turned down

parts.note: refuse is household rubbish, waste for the bin

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word ballad

explanation.surface: A poor song ended up being rejected.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn down an offer is to decline it; synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Station manager?

parts.note: a station is a TV or radio channel, and the handset that changes it manages it

explanation.definitionFit: The handheld controller for a television is used to switch channels from a distance.

clue.text: Bolt's very quick and keen on a regular basis

parts.note: fast means very quick

indicators.note: on a regular basis picks every other letter of the word keen

explanation.surface: Usain Bolt is very fast and consistently eager.
explanation.walkthrough: Usain Bolt the sprinter is the surface; the definition is the verb 'bolt', to secure a door.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolt a door is to secure it shut; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Awful fuss with clues, limiting compiler's first flourishing

awful suggests the letters are in a terrible state, rearranged
first points to the opening letter of the word compiler

explanation.surface: A setter fusses about bad clues while thriving.
explanation.definitionFit: Being successful means prospering or thriving; a synonym.

clue.text: Perished surrounding river — showing lack of water

indicators.note: surrounding means the synonym for perished goes round the river letter

parts.note: died means perished

explanation.surface: Something perished by a river, apparently from drought.

clue.text: Exhausted European member of parliament changed diet

indicators.note: changed says the letters of diet are rearranged

explanation.surface: A worn-out MP from Europe has altered what they eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exhausted has been used up completely, drained of its contents.

clue.text: Kill around four of those in management?

indicators.note: around means the word for kill is placed round the numeral

parts.note: to execute is to kill, especially by sentence of law
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to bump off a few bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: The executive is the body of senior managers running an organisation.

clue.text: Something spread on bread or crumpet

definitions.meaning: a smooth meat or fish paste spread on toast or bread
crumpet is old British slang for the head

explanation.walkthrough: A crumpet is also a British griddle cake eaten toasted, which misleads towards spreads.
explanation.definitionFit: Pâté is a savoury spread, and pate is an old word for the head or crown.

clue.text: Given description of the tower of Pisa?

definitions.text: description of the tower of Pisa?
definitions.meaning: the famous tower leans, sloping at an angle

clue.text: Polite place to buy savouries, cold, to get consumed

parts.note: a deli or delicatessen sells cooked meats and savoury food
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
ate is the past tense of eat, so consumed

explanation.surface: A courteous shop sells snacks that are cold but eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicate can mean tactful or diplomatic, handling a matter with polite care.

clue.text: Hippopotamus I captured holding rock, perhaps

indicators.note: holding says the clue words contain the answer within their run of letters

explanation.surface: A captured hippo apparently clutching a stone.

clue.text: The same one with depression? I almost cry

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

parts.note: to call is to cry out

clue.text: Some turned out great — or dreadful

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown into a new order, as in 'out of shape'

explanation.surface: A review saying some results were either brilliant or awful.

clue.text: Caught after Sid's criminal record

criminal suggests the letters of Sid are bent into a wrong shape

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sid's criminal record' reads as a rap sheet; 'record' is the vinyl kind, and 'criminal' rearranges SID into DIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a gramophone record, the flat vinyl kind played on a turntable.

clue.text: Chewing the fat, the cat's upset by call

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the word cat, its 's meaning is
to ring is to call on the telephone

explanation.surface: A cat is upset by a phone call while gnawing on fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chewing the fat' is an idiom for gossiping or talking idly.
explanation.definitionFit: Chewing the fat means chatting at length, so idle talk or gossip.

clue.text: Doctor Sam on this hospital dept creating surprise

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A medic called Sam working in a hospital unit causes amazement.
explanation.definitionFit: Astonishment is great surprise or amazement; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Controlling Aida, perhaps, with the sound of a bell

parts.note: Aida is a Verdi opera, an example of one
ting is the light ringing note of a small bell

explanation.surface: Performing Verdi's Aida to the ringing of a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate a machine is to control or run it.

clue.text: Some temp has Israeli accent

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A temporary office worker speaks with an Israeli accent.
explanation.definitionFit: An accent is stress placed on a syllable or word, a synonym for stress.

clue.text: Who flogs beer carried by ship? One on board

indicators.note: carried by means the drinks sit inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
ales are beers
a man is a piece on a chess or draughts board

explanation.surface: A man who sells beer is shipped aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' is British slang for sell, not whip.
explanation.definitionFit: A salesman sells goods, and to flog is informal for selling.

clue.text: Sizes of certain players in foreign teams

indicators.note: in places the two synonyms inside the rearranged word teams
foreign suggests the letters of teams are made strange, rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' rearranges TEAMS into MEATS, which then splits open to take SUREMEN inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Measurements are the recorded dimensions or sizes of something, such as clothing sizes.

clue.text: Give him a nag in the inn?

definitions.text: Give him a nag in the inn?

parts.words: Give him a nag in the inn?
parts.note: a nag is a horse, handed to the groom at an inn rather than a scold

explanation.definitionFit: An ostler is a stableman at an inn who looks after guests' horses.

clue.text: Coy? Not fantastic word to describe Lord Sugar

clue.text: Watch the man had heard

parts.note: the man is he, and had shortens to 'd, so together he'd

clue.text: Without thinking, start to comment: 'Are the French sneaky?'

parts.note: taken as written
les is French for 'the' in the plural
sly means sneaky or underhand

clue.text: Calm lake — good place for a picture

parts.note: to ease is to calm or soothe

clue.text: One shows arrogance from heads of state? Not one bit

indicators.note: heads of picks the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.definitionFit: A snob looks down on people thought socially inferior, showing haughty disdain.

flipping says the pronoun for the setter is turned back to front

clue.text: John is after one good place to stay in the far north

clue.text: Small and secure thing to use in a flood

definitions.text: thing to use in a flood

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
taken as written
to bag something is to secure or obtain it

explanation.surface: Advice on keeping a small thing safe when floodwater rises.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacks filled with sand are piled up as a barrier against floodwater.

clue.text: It's designed to detain criminal longer, I'll be bound
